_doc: Known panel-vs-browser differences check.py accepts (format: scripts/screenshots/checks.py). Every entry says why. Measured against main with the browser drawing the panel's Roboto; bounds are the largest offset seen plus a few px. Fixed a gap on the panel? Tighten or delete its entry (check.py lists entries a run didn't need). Never widen an entry to make a PR pass without saying so in the PR.

offsets.reason: Box shape, not position: the rail's name labels are 88 px wide cells with the name centred, the browser box is the name itself (Δx ≈ −(88 − w) / 2, Δw = 88 − w).
Avatar initials: the panel centres one glyph in a label as tall as the avatar's font line; the browser box is the glyph's CSS line box (Δh 8–18 px). The avatars themselves line up.
Box shape: the panel's @here text is a row of word labels ending in a cut '…' label; the browser box ends at its ellipsis (Δw).
The big clock: .dash-clock is line-height 1 on a 102.4 px font, the panel's label is the 104 px font's own line (Δh −18, Δy +8–12); the digits shown change the width.
Message line with an emoji: the panel splits it into a label per word plus a picture; the run of labels is a few px narrower than the browser's text box (Δw).

Box shape: a message whose emoji wraps to a second line — the browser's text box spans both lines, the panel's words are one line with the picture under them (Δh); the run of word labels is a little narrower (Δw).
Small labels whose CSS line box and the panel's font line differ by a few px (badges, headings, the date).

The today timeline's 'now' marker moves with the clock (~1 px a minute and between refreshes): panel and browser draw it from fetches up to 30 s apart and round its position differently. Seen 9 px apart in CI.

offsets.reason: Box shape: the offline note's label spans the note on the panel, the browser box is the sentence (Δw).

offsets.reason: Wrapped / cut message text: the panel's word labels or wrapped label break the lines at slightly different words (the hinted glyphs are narrower), so the longest line differs (Δw).
Sticky notes: the panel's hinted glyphs are a little narrower, so a note's text can break at other words — its longest line differs (Δw) and it can be a line shorter (Δh).

A stale spot's '⏱ last seen …': one inline run in the browser, so a second line starts under the ⏱ and the text box at the ⏱; on the panel the ⏱ is a picture beside the wrapped label (Δx = the ⏱ and its space).

offsets.reason: Box shape: the hint's and the date's CSS line boxes are 40 px taller than the panel's font lines (the night layout's big line-height).
Night clock and the 'Tomorrow' line: font line vs CSS line box, the light 200 weight's digits.
Lock screen header: the household name, the clock's light digits and the date come out a little narrower or wider than Chromium's (hinted glyphs at 24–160 px).

texts.reason: The browser's lock page has an Unlock submit button for the tablet's form; the panel unlocks from its own PIN button.
The browser renders its PIN pad (hidden behind the summary) on the lock screen already; the panel builds the pad when 'PIN' is tapped.
Zone names on the map are HTML labels in the browser, drawn into the map picture on the panel.
